Extract named entities from texts using spaCy

Source: R/spacy_extract_entity.R
spacy_extract_entity.Rd

This function extracts named entities from texts, based on the entity tag ent attributes of documents objects parsed by spaCy (see https://spacy.io/usage/linguistic-features#named-entities).

Usage

spacy_extract_entity(
  x,
  output = c("data.frame", "list"),
  type = c("all", "named", "extended"),
  multithread,
  n_process = 1L,
  batch_size = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a character object or a TIF-compliant corpus data.frame (see https://github.com/ropensci/tif)

output

type of returned object, either "list" or "data.frame".

type

type of named entities, either named, extended, or all. Extended entities are those of types DATE, TIME, PERCENT, MONEY, QUANTITY, ORDINAL and CARDINAL, and named entities are those of all other types. The entity types are those of the language model; see its "Label scheme" on https://spacy.io/models.

multithread

deprecated; it no longer has any effect, and gives a warning if supplied. Documents are always processed in batches with spaCy's nlp.pipe(); use n_process and batch_size instead.

n_process

the number of processes for spaCy's nlp.pipe() to use: 1 (the default) processes the documents in the current R session's Python process, a larger number starts that many Python processes, and -1 uses all CPUs. Starting the processes and loading the model in each takes time, so more than one process helps only for large numbers of documents. A custom pipeline component must be defined in an importable Python module to be used in other processes.

batch_size

the number of documents that spaCy's nlp.pipe() processes together; NULL (the default) uses the pipeline's default (nlp.batch_size). Larger batches can be faster, but use more memory.

...

unused

Value

either a list or data.frame of tokens

Details

When the option output = "data.frame" is selected, the function returns a data.frame with the following fields.

entity_type

type of entity (e.g. ORG for organizations)

start_id

serial number ID of starting token. This number corresponds with the number of data.frame returned from spacy_tokenize(x) with default options.

length

number of words (tokens) included in a named entity (e.g. for an entity, "New York Stock Exchange"", length = 4)

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
spacy_initialize()

txt <- c(doc1 = "The Supreme Court is located in Washington D.C.",
         doc2 = "Paul earned a postgraduate degree from MIT.")
spacy_extract_entity(txt)
spacy_extract_entity(txt, output = "list")
} # }
